newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays weak on offshore dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays weak on offshore dollar demand.

text.p: The ringgit remained weak against the dollar in early Asian trading on continued buying of the dollar by offshore players, dealers said.
"There's good offshore buying around 2.5190 and dollar/ringgit should break through the 2.5200 level again today, possibly to 2.5240," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the dollar demand was due to mid-year book closing and some window dressing activities.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5195/5205 a dollar, unchanged from its close in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday. It hit a low of 2.5220 during London trading overnight.
Dealers said they expected the ringgit to stay weak through the week although fears of central bank intervention would cap the dollar's rise.
Bank Negara was unlikely to intervene if the ringgit stayed close to the 2.5200 level, they said.
"After the mid-year book close, we should see the ringgit go back to around the 2.51 level," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
